subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should portable Agent Bundles be a first-party core CLI/import contract, a plugin or bundle-style package backed by new core APIs, or part of the broader same-product migration and per-agent restore design?
rationale: The answer affects CLI namespace, config writes, workspace import safety, skill install behavior, channel bindings, model settings, environment requirements, and the archive trust boundary.

options.title: Design a scoped core contract
options.body: Define a dry-run-first core Agent Bundle manifest and import/export lifecycle with explicit portable fields, secret exclusions, overwrite/rollback behavior, and regression coverage.

options.title: Fold into migration and restore
options.body: Treat this as a sub-scope of same-product migration and per-agent restore before adding separate `agents bundle` commands.

options.title: Expose plugin APIs and route to ClawHub
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only missing safe APIs, then let bundle-style plugins or ClawHub packages own optional agent packages.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped core contract
recommendation.body: Define a dry-run-first core Agent Bundle manifest and import/export lifecycle with explicit portable fields, secret exclusions, overwrite/rollback behavior, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses agent routing/config and backup/import safety, both areas tied to gumadeiras in the observed history.
